packet.close.what: put the open packet away, which is also what stops the per-tick rebuild that keeps an open one live
packet.close.answers: Nothing comes back, whether or not a packet was open: the answer is null and the call cannot fail.

packet.open.what: dissect one transmission and gather what every node did with it, and leave it as the packet the view keeps following while its message is still spreading

params.name: id
params.what: the transmission's id; absent or zero is refused

params.name: seek
params.what: step this many ids at a time until a transmission that is still in the ledger is found, up to fifty tries, which is what the previous and next arrows send; absent means take the given id or nothing

packet.open.answers: `id` is the transmission actually opened, which is not the one asked for when `seek` walked to a neighbouring one. `transmissions` counts every time the message was put on the air, so a relayed flood is told from a single advert without reading the header, and `reached` is how many distinct nodes heard any of them. Refused where no engine is built, and where nothing of that id is left in the event log.

example.what: open the first transmission of a run
